inputs.text:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: final industrial-design presentation board, one coherent landscape image file
Primary request: Show one resolved compact desktop enclosure for a Raspberry Pi 5 music workstation called SHR-DAW. This is the only concept: a manufacturable small wedge console, overall proportions about 132 mm wide × 118 mm deep × 82 mm high at the rear and about 38 mm at the front. Its 4-inch landscape screen is inset into the sloping top at exactly 24 degrees above the desk, rising away from the operator so it faces forward. The enclosure has an extended rear downstand/heel that reaches the desk and makes the unit level and stable.
Scene/backdrop: clean warm-light-gray industrial design studio background and tabletop, no props, no hands.
Subject and form: charcoal textured PC-ABS upper shell, dark graphite folded-aluminum bottom/rear spine, warm gray horizontal grille inserts, subtle off-white accent line. Restrained character of a compact modern digital console with a faint analog-console influence; coherent, compact, no decorative pastiche.
Composition/framing: one presentation board containing one large front-right three-quarter hero view plus one smaller rear three-quarter inset of the exact same product on the same canvas. Keep both views large and clearly readable. The hero must clearly show the inclined landscape screen, uninterrupted front intake, right-side recessed connector bay, left control cheek, rear heel, and four low rubber feet. The rear inset must clearly show the 40 mm exhaust grille and recessed rear cable hood.
Front details: two continuous horizontal louvered intake bands across the front fascia, sized as real ventilation and kept unobstructed; rounded slot ends; no controls in front of the vents. The intake aligns with internal upper and lower air channels. A narrow left cheek beside the display carries exactly five small low-profile cream-colored square buttons in a vertical row, without text or symbols.
Screen: active area approximately 86 × 52 mm within a 97 × 58.5 mm display module, landscape. Show a tasteful dark terminal-style music workstation interface: abstract grid, tracker lanes, meters, and small blocks, but no readable words, no logos, no brand marks, no fake labels, no touchscreen gestures. The interface must be right-way-up to an operator standing in front and not rotated upside-down.
Right connector bay: one realistic recessed, shadowed side pocket exposing exactly four USB-A receptacles arranged as two vertical pairs and one RJ45 Ethernet receptacle, with enough surrounding wall and a small adjacent reusable cable-tie slot. Do not depict USB-C in this side bay. Ports must be realistically scaled and cut into a planar internal bracket, not floating.
Rear inset details: one circular 40 mm fan exhaust behind a horizontal-slot finger guard on the left half of the rear; one recessed open-bottom cable hood on the right half with exactly one USB-C power inlet and exactly two smaller micro-HDMI openings, plus a small round native power-button actuator. Show cables absent. The rear wall extends down to the tabletop and includes a small stand-off bumper so the exhaust cannot sit flush against a wall.
Mechanical realism: visible part lines for upper bezel, lower shell, and metal base; a few small black captive screws on underside/rear only; 2–3 mm wall visual thickness; radiused edges; realistic grille depth; no impossible overhangs; no exposed circuit boards; no transparent shell; no handle; no knobs; no speakers; no audio jacks; no extra ports.
Lighting/mood: polished premium product visualization, soft directional studio light, accurate matte plastic and powder-coated metal textures, restrained shadows, realistic scale.
Constraints: exactly one product design and exactly one image file; the smaller view is an inset of the same product, not an alternate. Preserve the specified port identities and counts. No dimension annotations, callout arrows, legends, captions, logos, watermarks, or readable text. Avoid unsupported labels and impossible connector geometry.
